data.description:
Board request, DM msg 163, 2026-08-30 20:41Z, verbatim: "Also, I'm going to be using this on my phone so let's make it layout mobile friendly". Context: the board member's primary interface with the company is this chat app (CLAUDE.md), and he will use it from a phone — mobile is a first-class surface, not a nice-to-have.

Scope — what 'mobile friendly' means for this app: the web UI at apps/chat/public must be usable on a phone-sized viewport (~375-430px wide). Concretely: (1) responsive layout — the sidebar (channels + DM roster) must not consume the viewport; collapse it behind a toggle/drawer on narrow screens, with the message pane full-width; (2) touch targets and font sizes adequate for touch (no tiny click zones); (3) viewport meta + no horizontal scroll; (4) compose box usable with the on-screen keyboard (doesn't get hidden, input stays visible); (5) the AS-9 URL-state contract keeps working so links shared from phone/desktop open the same view.

Relationship to the other chat UX tasks (all bumped per board msg 160 "let's get going on all the chat UX improvements"): AS-17 (thread scroll position + default identity) is independent. AS-18 (DM pinning/sort) touches the same sidebar this task collapses — coordinate, land AS-18 after or fold its sidebar markup in. AS-19 (threads inline or large modal, retiring the narrow thread sidebar) INTERACTS directly: the thread presentation chosen there determines the mobile thread UX (a modal is naturally full-screen on mobile; inline needs its own narrow-viewport treatment). Sequence AS-19 before this task so the mobile layout is built against the final thread presentation, not the retiring sidebar.

Acceptance: chat is fully usable — read, switch conversations, post, open threads, mark read — in a 390px-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll; desktop layout unchanged.
data.title: Chat UI: mobile-friendly responsive layout

data.body: Filed on behalf of human:forrest from DM msg 163 (2026-08-30). Full decision context and scope in the description. Position 3 in the chat UX queue: AS-17 -> AS-19 -> AS-23 -> AS-18; AS-19's thread-presentation decision is a deliberate prerequisite.

Plan written (agent:cto-owen). Approach: one mobile breakpoint at <=700px — #sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer (fixed, translateX(-100%), scrim at z 25 / drawer z 26, below the AS-19 backdrop z 30), hamburger in #conv-header, drawer closes on any conversation select (single hook in selectConversation) and never touches the URL (AS-9 projection invariant intact). Touch: (hover:none) unhides .message .actions — hover-gated 'reply in thread' is a functional break on touch, not polish; 40px targets; 16px input font kills iOS focus auto-zoom. Keyboard: 100dvh + a ~12-line visualViewport pin (--app-height) because no CSS unit tracks the iOS keyboard; honestly flagged as device-verifiable only. Global: overflow-x hidden, task-panel width clamped via min(). SCOPE DECISION: Priya's AS-19 backlog item (selection-drag from dialog to backdrop closes the modal) FOLDS IN — same three files, and press-drag selection is the canonical mobile gesture; fix is her sketched pointerdown-target check as a NEW pure predicate (existing thread-modal.js exports and their tests byte-unmodified; test additions only). No separate task filed. Guarded suites: url-state.test.js + scroll.test.js byte-identical to master, thread-modal.test.js additive-only. Acceptance split honestly: A1-A3 container-assertable (served HTML/CSS rules, suites), B1-B8 board phone walk (~2 min, iPhone/Tailscale) — the board IS the mobile QA; checklist written for him verbatim in the plan. Desktop invariance: every new rule inside media/hover guards except three named no-op-at-desktop lines. Sequencing: AS-18 rebases trivially (this touches sidebar positioning, not list contents).

Implementation complete (agent:developer-marcus), 2 commits on feat/AS-23-mobile-layout (2a904f3 selection-drag fix, 31550f2 mobile layout). Suite 136 green in-container (was 132; +3 predicate tests, +1 served-artifact test); also verified via throwaway container on port 8399 (live 8347 untouched). Guards hold: url-state.test.js + scroll.test.js byte-identical to master, thread-modal.test.js purely additive (0 removed lines), existing exports byte-unmodified, STATIC_FILES unchanged. Two boring choices where the plan was ambiguous: (1) drawer close in selectConversation is gated on url==='push' — the 5s poll funnels through selectConversation with url:'none' and an unconditional close would slam a drawer the user is browsing every 5s; 'push' is exactly the set of user picks (sidebar li, roster row, typeahead, new-channel). (2) #conv-header becomes a wrapping flex row at <=700px (toggle+title line one, purpose full-width below) — the plan added the toggle to the header but not its layout; no markup beyond the planned button. Note for QA on A3: two additional top-level rules exist beyond the three named — default display:none for the NEW #sidebar-toggle/#sidebar-scrim elements; they only hide new elements, zero effect on desktop layout. Board-only residual: B1-B8 phone checklist (iOS keyboard behavior is device-only-verifiable; code degrades to 100dvh without visualViewport).

QA review (agent:qa-priya), cold, branch feat/AS-23-mobile-layout @ 6f5af77 vs master.

VERDICT: PASS. No inline fixes needed; nothing trivial found to fix. Recommend done + merge; B1-B8 hand off to the board.

A1 PASS — node --test in fresh container (compose -p asc-chat-qa23, test profile, mountless): 136/136 green, matches claim (132 + 3 predicate + 1 artifact). Guards: url-state.test.js, scroll.test.js, server.js all 0-line diff vs master; thread-modal.test.js numstat 39/0 (purely additive); thread-modal.js 25/0 (pure append — existing exports byte-unmodified).
A2 PASS — re-verified independently against a throwaway container (image asc-chat-qa23-test, port 8399, no volume mounts, live 8347 untouched, stopped after): served HTML carries viewport-fit=cover, id=sidebar-toggle, id=sidebar-scrim; served CSS carries the 700px block, translateX(-100%), hover:none, 100dvh, --app-height (2 hits, +2 in app.js), overflow-x:hidden, safe-area-inset-bottom, min(300px, calc(100vw - 32px)); zero bare 'width: 300px'; content-type text/css.
A3 PASS — full CSS diff walked: every new rule sits inside (max-width:700px) or (hover:none) except five top-level changes: the three named (dvh cascade on #app, body overflow-x, task-panel min() clamp) plus the two disclosed in deviation 3 (display:none defaults for the NEW #sidebar-toggle/#sidebar-scrim). All five are desktop no-ops; no other selector touches the new elements outside the media block. AS-19's 600px sheet rules unedited.

DEVIATIONS (3) — all judged sound:
1. Drawer close gated on url==='push': CORRECT and necessary. Traced every selectConversation caller — 'push' (default) is exactly the user-pick set: sidebar li (L204), roster DM existing/new (L268/L296), DM typeahead (L509), new-channel (L674). url:'none' is exactly poll (L735), send re-render (L553), restoreFromUrl (L622). Without the gate the 5s poll would slam an open drawer every tick. Phone deep-link traced: restore selects with 'none' (drawer already closed in markup — no class, scrim hidden), then the one-time auto-open runs after await restoreFromUrl and sees state.currentConv set → does not open. A deep link lands drawer-closed on the right conversation, no flash. AS-9 invariant intact: syncUrl/restoreFromUrl unedited, drawer state never in URL.
2. #conv-header wrapping flex row at <=700px: fills a real plan gap, fully media-guarded, desktop header untouched. Accepted.
3. Two extra top-level display:none rules: verified new-elements-only, disclosed up front. Accepted.

ATTACK (all clean):
- Backdrop gesture: tap down+up on backdrop closes (down===currentTarget); selection drag dialog→backdrop does not; drag backdrop→dialog does not (click target is dialog); stale pointerdown is cleared per click and overwritten per gesture — the only residual path (pointercancel, then a synthetic no-pointer click on the overlay) fails SAFE (refuses to close); null/undefined falls back to legacy.
- Z-order at phone width with a t= deep link: modal 30 > drawer 26 > scrim 25; sheet sits over the drawer. dm-options (20) joins the drawer stacking context, correct.
- --app-height pin: window.scrollTo(0,0) is window-level only; AS-17 preservation is pane-element scrollTop (scroll.js L43-47) — no interaction, and the window has no scrollable overflow to yank anyway.
- Horizontal scroll >700px: no new bare widths; only guarded rules plus the five no-ops. Drawer-open class residue after widening past 700px is inert (no unguarded rule references it; scrim display:none top-level).
- #sidebar-scrim[hidden]{display:none} correctly restores hidden semantics over the author display:block. Drawer is opaque (#3f0e40) and scrolls (overflow-y:auto).

BACKLOG (does not violate any stated criterion; not blocking): (a) drawer a11y polish — aria-expanded on #sidebar-toggle, Escape closes the open drawer; (b) popstate leaves an open drawer open (defensible as view-local state; note only).

BOARD PHONE WALK — B1-B8 remain open by design (iPhone over Tailscale, after the live server picks up the merge), restated verbatim from the plan:
B1. Open the chat. No sideways scrolling or pinch-zoom weirdness, in portrait or after rotating and back.
B2. The channel list is not squeezing the messages; on a fresh open with no conversation, the drawer greets you. Tap the hamburger in the header — the drawer slides in; tap the dimmed area — it closes without changing anything.
B3. Tap a channel in the drawer — the drawer closes itself and the channel fills the width. Rows are comfortably tappable.
B4. Tap the message box. The keyboard opens and the box stays visible above it — no zoom-in jump, no hidden composer. Type and send; Send is easy to hit. Dismiss the keyboard; layout settles back. (iOS keyboard behavior is device-only-verifiable; code degrades to 100dvh without visualViewport.)
B5. On any message, 'reply in thread' is visible without any hover and tappable. The thread opens full-screen; reply from in there too (B4 applies to the thread composer as well).
B6. In a thread with long text, long-press and drag a text selection that ends on the dimmed edge of the screen — the thread does NOT close. The x still closes it.
B7. Paste /?c=board&t=113 into the phone browser — right channel, thread sheet open (AS-9 on mobile). Back button closes the thread.
B8. Glance at desktop after all this: nothing moved.
